mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X gives N items to Y', immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's count, using the counts as they exist at that point.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: After 'X gives N items to Y', leaving X's count unchanged and not adding N to Y.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order of A and B.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement of the form 'X has K more than Y'.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Swapping A and B, treating it as B − A = K.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have', set up the equation (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order of C and D.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Interpreting the right‑hand side as |C − D| or as D − C.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement 'A has N items' fixes A's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a direct count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Treating the count as an initial value regardless of earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations, simplify, and propagate the information to reduce the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving any equation that determines a variable.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Solving for a variable but failing to substitute its value into other pending equations.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and difference equations—to ensure no contradictions.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the end of solving, before outputting the answer.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Accepting a solution that violates a transfer constraint, such as a giver ending up with a negative count.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing any comparative or difference‑equality statement.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Using a person's original count for a comparison that occurs after they have given away items.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through a chain of dependencies, and solve only that subsystem.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, to reduce the problem size.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Solving the entire system, including unrelated variables, leading to unnecessary complexity and potential errors.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if the names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similar names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the list of statements to create variables.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Merging 'Marlene' and 'Marilyn' into a single variable.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When parsing a statement of the form 'The number of items that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of items that A and B have', interpret the right‑hand side as the signed difference A − B, preserving the order of A and B as they appear; do not treat it as an absolute value or swap the order.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a difference‑equality statement includes the phrase 'difference between the number of ... that A and B have'.
mathgap.example: Incorrect: Interpreting 'the difference between the number of tomatoes that Patricia and Michael have' as |Patricia − Michael| or as Michael − Patricia, leading to wrong equations.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than"
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may focus on the phrase 'more than' and mistakenly reverse the subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map 'has K more than' to A − B = K, preserving the order of the names.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The word 'difference' sounds symmetric, leading the model to assume an absolute value.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'difference between' as a signed subtraction preserving order, not as an absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat transfers as independent of the narrative sequence.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer immediately when encountered, before any later statements that involve the participants.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat 'has N' as a starting condition rather than a snapshot.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'has N' as fixing the count at that point in the narrative, after any prior transfers.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model conflates the non‑negative K with the sign of the difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that while K is non‑negative, the expression A − B can be negative in equations that equate differences.
